cf.title: Injection point: fix race condition between attach and cleanup

input.subject: Injection point: fix race condition between attach and cleanup

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection stops the proposal at levels 1 or 2. The race is real and the 0001 spec reproduces it; the test-only fix leaves it in the module. demand-1 and standards-compat-1 are both fixable: the thread names one failing test as the consumer of a new core API, and names no branch for either fix. A committer who knows injection points must choose between the two fixes, which the author asks for in message #1.

brief.title: Injection points: detach local points by handle to fix a cleanup race
brief.problem: The injection_points test module removes points attached after injection_points_set_local() in a before_shmem_exit callback, and finds them only by name. If another backend detaches the point and attaches a new callback under the same name before the first backend exits, that cleanup detaches the new callback. The author reports that this makes the test 010_index_concurrently_upsert fail at times.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds InjectionPointHandle, which records the shared-memory slot and its generation for one attach call. InjectionPointDetachByHandle() detaches the callback only while the handle still matches, so a stale cleanup cannot remove a later callback. The test module stores handles for local points and detaches by handle at exit, and the name-based interfaces stay unchanged.
user_visible_surface: C API: new function InjectionPointAttachWithHandle(name, library, function, private_data, private_data_size, handle).
C API: new function InjectionPointDetachByHandle(handle), which returns false if that callback is already detached.
Docs: xfunc.sgml documents the two new functions.
Tests: new isolation spec local_cleanup in the injection_points module, which reproduces the race.
author_claims: The race can detach a callback that another backend attached later under the same name.
The 0001 isolation spec reproduces the race.
The fix leaves the existing name-based attach and detach interfaces unchanged.
A smaller fix only for 010_index_concurrently_upsert waits until cleanup is done; it was posted as a nocfbot patch.
brief.thread_state: Only the author has posted, in three messages: the first proposal and two v2 reposts to fix cfbot and a bad attachment. No reviewer has replied, and the author asks for a choice between the core API fix and the test-only fix.
unclear: The material does not say if the handle API is meant for extensions outside the test module, or only for injection_points.
The proposal does not say how the generation counter behaves on slot reuse or wraparound.
The thread does not say if the fix should be back-patched, or which branches carry the failing test.
The nocfbot test-only fix is not in v2, so its current state is not shown.
The material does not say if a race also exists for points that are not local.

prior_attempts.title: Disable installcheck for tap and regress tests for injection_points module
prior_attempts.quote: Disabling the test hides the problem, it does not fix it.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew the entry after noting that runningcheck was already disabled for the injection_points isolation tests in the tree, which covered most of the patch. Earlier, Michael Paquier objected that the crash may point to a real bug and that disabling the tests hides it. The author replied that the cause is injection_points shared memory setup during abort, but no fix for that cause was agreed in the thread.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P4 turned off installcheck for the injection_points tests to avoid a crash in shared memory setup during abort. This proposal fixes a different race, in the cleanup of local points, and addresses its cause in the module.

objections.title: New core API has one consumer while a test-only fix exists
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds InjectionPointAttachWithHandle() and InjectionPointDetachByHandle() to core injection_point.c, and only the injection_points test module ever calls them. Later work on injection_point.c must keep the slot and generation rules behind the handle intact, though only one cleanup path depends on them.
objections.argument: The material shows one concrete failure: 010_index_concurrently_upsert fails at times (message #1). Message #1 also offers a test-only fix that waits for cleanup, and the author asks reviewers to choose between the two. No other test, extension or user is named as needing to detach by handle, and the docs present it as a general API. A committer would likely ask whether more than one test is exposed before taking the larger fix.
objections.author_must_show: Which tests or extensions besides 010_index_concurrently_upsert use injection_points_set_local() in a way that can hit this race, and how would the test-only fix leave them exposed?

critic.reasoning: The 0001 spec shows the race is in the module's cleanup, so the test-only fix leaves it in place. But the material names only one failing test, and the author asks reviewers to choose between the two fixes.

objections.title: Core API addition does not say which branches get the fix
objections.failure_scenario: 010_index_concurrently_upsert keeps failing at times on the buildfarm in a stable branch. A committer must then either back-patch a new exported type and two functions in injection_point.h, or apply the test-only fix there. Master and the back branches then clean up local points in different ways.
objections.argument: The fix adds a new public C type and two functions to backend code to fix a race in a test module. The thread does not say which branches carry the failing test or the local-point cleanup, so the cost of the core change in stable branches is unknown. The author offers a test-only alternative but does not say whether it is meant for the back branches, which would mean two fixes for one race. A committer would likely ask for this plan before taking on new API in core.
objections.author_must_show: Which branches have this race, and which fix, the handle API or the nocfbot test change, goes into each of them?

critic.reasoning: The thread offers two fixes and names no branch for either. Injection points exist only in builds configured with them, and new functions do not break ABI, so the back-branch cost is likely small, but the plan is still missing.

touch_points.reason: The thread does not say which branches have the race, and a back-patch would add a new type and two functions.

questions: Which tests or extensions besides 010_index_concurrently_upsert use injection_points_set_local() in a way that can hit this race?
Which branches have this race, and which fix, the handle API or the nocfbot test change, goes into each of them?
Is the handle API meant for extensions outside the injection_points test module, or only for that module?
How does the generation counter behave when a slot is reused many times, including on wraparound?
Does the same race exist for points that are not local, when two backends detach and attach the same name?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the injection point code in injection_point.c and the injection_points test module. The author copied two people from the original thread; neither has replied.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new documented C type and two functions in core, and for the slot and generation rules behind them. The code exists only in builds with injection points enabled, so the exposure is limited to test builds.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted two corrected versions within a day to fix cfbot and a bad attachment, and asks for feedback on which fix to pursue.

priority.reason: The patch fixes a reproducible race that makes a test fail at times, and it benefits developers who write tests with local injection points. It is about 13 KiB, touches one core file, and keeps the name-based interfaces unchanged.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review cannot check whether the shared-memory slot layout changes, how the generation counter handles slot reuse, or whether the handle check and the detach happen under one lock.

precedents_retrieved.title: Persist injection points across server restarts
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a flush function to the injection_points test module that writes the attached injection points to a file, and the module reloads them into shared memory at startup through shared_preload_libraries. TAP tests could then make a process such as the checkpointer wait at an early startup phase, before any SQL connection is possible.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis found the complexity large for one use case, and Andres Freund doubted the direction because tests needing injection points before consistency must be written in C anyway and can attach points in their own shared_preload_libraries entry. The author proposed a postmaster GUC listing points to load instead, then withdrew the patch since one known use case was perhaps not enough.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Tests that require
injection points before consistency also can't wait for injection points using
the SQL interface or such, so most of the stuff has to be written in C
anyway. And if so, you also can attach to injection points in the relevant
shared_preload_libraries entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Backpatching injection point core facilities to REL_17_STABLE
precedents_retrieved.summary: Michael Paquier proposed backpatching core injection point APIs to REL_17_STABLE: cached points and loading for critical sections, IS_INJECTION_POINT_ATTACHED(), and runtime arguments. The goal was to make tests easier to port and to keep the facility consistent across stable branches, with v18 cherry-picks suggested later as a first step.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane objected only to pushing such changes just before a release freeze and to touching v13, and Michael Paquier agreed. No later message records the withdrawal or its reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Some refactoring for fixed-numbered stats template in injection_points
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch refactors the fixed-numbered pgstats template in injection_stats_fixed.c. It replaces the single routine that increments the counters with a series of routines whose internals sit in a macro, as in pgstatfuncs.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The author withdrew the entry, and only the opening message is shown, with no replies. The author called the change a matter of personal taste.

precedents_retrieved.title: Disable installcheck for tap and regress tests for injection_points module
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch turns off installcheck (running-server mode) for the TAP and isolation tests of the injection_points module in the meson build, as was already done for its regression tests. The author found that even a local injection point in one backend can crash an unrelated backend that triggers the point during transaction abort, because GetNamedDSMSegment is then called after resource release has started.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after noting that runningcheck was already disabled for the injection_points isolation tests in the tree, which covered most of the patch. Earlier, Michael Paquier objected that the crash may point to a real bug and that disabling the tests hides it. The author replied that the cause is injection_points shared memory setup during abort, but no fix for that cause was agreed in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Disabling the test hides the problem, it does not fix it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: BUG #18741: Detaching a partition referencing a partitioned table fails with a trigger-related error
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alexander Lakhin reported that detaching a partition fails with an internal trigger error when the partition has a foreign key to a partitioned table and its new parent has no matching foreign key. Tender Wang and jian he discussed fixing this, mainly by rejecting such ATTACH PARTITION commands except where the partition references a non-partitioned table or its own parent's hierarchy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They contain the bug report and two design suggestions with no patch, review or decision, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY support for partitioned indexes. It changes index_drop() to expand a partitioned index into the list of its partition indexes and run the concurrent drop steps on all of them in two transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier disliked the new code path for deleting dependent objects in the partition tree and said the problem needed more design work first. The patch then stopped applying to HEAD, and the author withdrew it until the related patch for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned tables makes progress.

Looking

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables. It first creates catalog entries for all partition indexes as invalid, then builds and validates them the way REINDEX CONCURRENTLY does, so an interrupted run leaves INVALID indexes that DROP or REINDEX can clean up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages are reviews and fixes from mid-2024 with no stated objection, and in October 2024 a user asked why progress had stalled; the entry was withdrawn in April 2025 with no visible closing message.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejects this idea. The reason recorded for [P4] applies only to the nocfbot test-only fix in message #1, which works around the race in one test and leaves it in the module; the main proposal (0002) fixes the cause.

From the standards and compatibility angle the proposal is small. It keeps the name-based interfaces and adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog entry or dump state. The only open point is which branches get which fix.

From this angle the proposal has nothing to object to. Injection point state lives only in shared memory, is rebuilt at every server start, and is never written to WAL, relation files or catalogs, so pg_upgrade, standbys and subscribers do not see it. The patch adds a type and two functions to injection_point.h and leaves the existing name-based attach and detach functions as they are, so no current extension call breaks. Without the code, two points cannot be checked: whether the shared-memory slot layout changes, and whether a back-patch would change anything beyond adding these functions.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Injection points are a test facility that only works in builds with injection points enabled, and the new handle API changes no privilege, adds no SQL-callable surface and exposes no data. A stale handle can only fail to detach, so it gives no new way to affect other sessions.

From the maintenance-and-fit angle there is no objection. The new API exists only in builds with injection points enabled, so it costs nothing on any hot path. It fixes a real race in name-based detach, it is optional, and the existing interfaces stay unchanged. The only open point is committability: no committer has replied yet, and the author asks whether a core API fix or a test-only fix is preferred. A committer would likely ask whether the handle is meant for out-of-core extensions, since that decides how stable it has to stay. That needs an answer, but it is not a failure scenario. [P4] concerns installcheck crashes in the same module and does not apply here.

No existing core feature, contrib module or external tool detaches one specific injection point callback safely; InjectionPointDetach() only matches by name, which is the race itself. The author's test-only fix stabilizes 010_index_concurrently_upsert but not the module, so whether the core handle API is worth adding is a desirability and design question for other angles.
The flaky test is real demand for some fix. The open point is whether that demand justifies a core API addition.
